newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open up as miners rebound.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open up as miners rebound.

text.p: The Australian share market opened up on Friday after a stronger finish on Wall Street added to the relatively firm local tone.
From opening, the All Ordinaries index added 10.7 points to 2,445.8.
After suffering significant selling on Thursday, major miners BHP and CRA led the way higher with the rest of the market also making gains in a continuation of Thursday's resilient performance.
"It's a good start and keeps yesterday afternoon's action going," said a Sydney broker.
"BHP and CRA are the big winners so far. They were overdone yesterday and RTZ had a good run overseas as well."
As with others, the broker suggested the pre-weekend malaise could set in later in the day with US payrolls out later today.
"I would look for it to come off later ahead of the weekend and with the U.S. labour force numbers due out. People will be careful ahead of those numbers," the broker said.
Helix Resources jumped ahead again, up 12 cents to A$4.82 (US$3.68) after gold major Acacia said it bought 17 percent of the Gawler Craton gold hopeful. Acacia shares lost 14 cents to A$2.25.

Victorian gold explorer Ballarat Goldfields topped turnover with 44.56 million shares traded, the bulk of it in one line of 44.46 million shares specialled through Hartley Poynton at a price of 7.1 cents per share.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to one, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
